title: Induction Intake Prompts
description: Suggestion-chip content for the induction terminal's Pages 7-8 (design/induction-terminal.md): gender-identity and pronoun suggestions, the banal texture questions, and bible §20's eight core questions verbatim. Every suggestion here is illustrative only, offered as a quick-start a player may click to insert into their own free-text answer -- never a real answer for any of the six actual kids (data/characters/kids/README.md). Singleton file: data/campaign/induction-intake-prompts.json.

genderIdentityOptions.description: Suggestion chips for Page 7's gender-identity field. Illustrative only -- the field is always free text too, and this list is deliberately not exhaustive.

pronounOptions.description: Suggestion chips for Page 7's pronouns field. Same free-text-always-available rule as genderIdentityOptions.

appearanceOptions.description: Suggestion chips for Page 7's appearance-notes field -- generic texture, not a real description of any of the six actual kids. Same free-text-always-available rule as genderIdentityOptions.

banalQuestions.description: Light texture questions, deliberately distinct in register from the Eight Questions below -- adding one is a pure data edit, no code change.

eightQuestions.description: ideas/story/blank-inheritance-v4.md §20's real intake quiz, verbatim -- DO NOT alter the `text` field's wording. Every answer becomes an Anchor, a side-plot seed, or a vulnerability (design/induction-terminal.md §1).

number.description: Eight Questions only -- display order 1-8, matching bible §20's own numbering.

text.description: The question itself, verbatim where it has a canonical bible source.

purposeNote.description: OOC framing for what this answer is used for, populated only where the bible states one explicitly (§20's own parenthetical notes) -- null elsewhere, never invented to make every entry look equally annotated.

suggestions.description: Illustrative answer chips. Clicking one inserts it into the free-text field; never binding, a player's own words always win.
